heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 can print Siraya Tech ABS-GF at speeds up to 179 mm/s within its 15 mm³/s volumetric limit, but it strictly requires swapping out the stock stainless steel nozzle for a hardened steel assembly. Additionally, because the A1 is an open-frame printer, drafting management or an enclosure is necessary to avoid catastrophic layer splitting and warp.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with PVP glue stick or liquid adhesive release barrier
slicerTweaks: Cap 'Max volumetric speed' at 15 mm³/s in OrcaSlicer filament settings to prevent under-extrusion at high linear speeds.
Enable a 5mm to 8mm outer brim with a 0mm brim-object gap to counteract high thermal contraction on open-bed prints.
Enable 'Draft Shield' under the Others tab to create a sacrificial perimeter wall that traps bed heat and deflects ambient drafts.
Disable the auxiliary fan entirely and set layer cooling fan to 0% for the first 4 layers, capping maximum fan speed at 15% for overhangs.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Rapid nozzle bore enlargement and irregular extrusion width
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: The abrasive glass fibers in Siraya Tech ABS-GF quickly ream out the factory stainless steel nozzle orifice.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Replace the stock hotend with an official Bambu Lab 0.4mm or 0.6mm Hardened Steel Hotend assembly.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe corner lifting and print detachment from the build surface
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Uncontrolled ambient drafts on the open-frame bed induce strong thermal contraction stresses in the ABS matrix.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Set bed temperature to 100°C, apply a uniform layer of liquid glue/glue stick, and enable OrcaSlicer's Draft Shield feature.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Interlayer splitting and delamination along the Z-axis
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling or low printing temperature preventing proper glass-transition fusion between layers.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Increase nozzle temperature to 265°C, lower max part cooling fan to 10%, and eliminate external room airflow.

faq.question: Can I print Siraya Tech ABS-GF with the stock Bambu Lab A1 out of the box?
faq.answer: No. The stock A1 includes a stainless steel nozzle that will wear out within hundreds of grams of abrasive glass-fiber filament. You must install a Bambu Hardened Steel hotend first.

faq.question: Is it safe to run Siraya Tech ABS-GF through the AMS Lite?
faq.answer: It is not recommended. The rigid, abrasive fibers will wear down the AMS Lite feeding funnels, internal gears, and standard PTFE tubing over time; use an external spool mount instead.

faq.question: What drying parameters should be used for this filament?
faq.answer: Dry Siraya Tech ABS-GF in a dedicated filament dryer at 70°C for 6 to 8 hours before printing to eliminate moisture-induced voiding, poor layer bonding, and stringing.

faq.question: How should I handle VOC emissions since the A1 has no chamber enclosure?
faq.answer: Because the A1 is open-frame, print only in a well-ventilated space, vent air externally with an exhaust duct, or enclose the printer using a tent equipped with an active carbon and HEPA filtration unit.
